summary: The scripts are good IELTS material: 718–855 words a part, natural speech, and real distractors in every part (the clerk guesses 'birthday', the Oak Room is ruled out, the walking club and council survey are set aside before the school class). The weak point was the question side: in Part 2, Part 3 and Part 4 many options and note lines repeated the script word for word, so students could match sounds instead of meaning. I reworded those options and note lines (answers and the audio unchanged), which brings the paper up to IELTS level and gives 37 of 40 questions a real paraphrase pair.
strengths: Correct four-part format: booking call (table completion), social monologue (MCQ + place matching), two-student discussion (MCQ + two pick-two items), lecture (ONE WORD notes).

Every MCQ in Parts 2 and 3 names the wrong options in the script before the right one (Q11–14, Q21–26), and Part 1 has self-corrections (Q2 birthday→retirement, Q3 16th→23rd, Q4 Oak→Willow, Q5 200→180).
Answers come in question order and gap answers are exactly as heard, within the word limits.
Script length suits real timing (Part 1 718, Part 2 830, Part 3 855, Part 4 790 words).

issues.problem: Part 2 matching box (Q15–20) repeated the script word for word: 'was brought here from another site', 'has a surface that wheelchairs can use', 'was paid for by a single donor', 'is closed to the public during the winter' all appear in the audio as printed. This makes the matching far easier than IELTS.
issues.change: Reworded options A–F (same letters, same keys): A 'was funded by one person', B 'is suitable for wheelchair users', C 'cannot be visited for part of the year', D 'is ideal for birdwatching', E 'has displays produced by young people', F 'was moved from its original location'. Explains updated; G and H distractors unchanged.

issues.problem: Part 4 notes copied the lecture almost word for word around several gaps (Q31 'burnt crumbs ... were found in a stone', Q36 'driven by', Q37 'the poor ate', Q39 'cheap ... removed', Q40 'an American sold').
issues.change: Reworded the note lines only: 'charred remains ... were discovered', 'the biggest Roman mills were powered by', 'eaten by the wealthy; poorer families lived on', 'inexpensive but stripped out', 'a US inventor marketed'. Gap answers unchanged and still exactly as heard.

issues.problem: Q27–28 correct options were the script's exact words ('how many times they woke', 'how they feel on waking'), and Q30's option 'test the diary on friends' likewise.
issues.change: Options now read 'the number of times their sleep was interrupted', 'their mood when they first get up', 'try the diary out on people they know'. Letters and keys unchanged.

issues.problem: Table text 'the largest of the three rooms' was the script's words, so the pair was identical words.
issues.change: Table now says 'the biggest room in the building'; pair ['it's the largest of the three', 'the biggest room in the building'].

issues.problem: Pair ['a deposit against damage', 'deposit against damage'] was the same words, and the question side was not even in the table.
issues.change: Pair is now ['it goes back to you within a week', 'returned within a week'].

issues.problem: Pair ['written entirely by children', 'written by children'] was the same words.
issues.change: With the reworded option: ['written entirely by children', 'produced by young people'].

issues.problem: Pair 'memory for sleep is famously bad' is not a paraphrase of 'relied on what people remembered'.
issues.change: Pair is now ['asked people at the end of the study', 'relied on what people remembered'].

issues.problem: Pair 'insisted on' / 'insist the study should include' was the same word.
issues.change: Pair is now ['how people function the following day', 'daytime alertness'].

issues.problem: Explain called Doctor Rahimov 'the tutor', but in the script the tutor is a woman ('when you showed her the draft'); Rahimov is a male researcher who supervises half the year.
issues.change: Explain now names Doctor Rahimov as the researcher everyone would assume suggested it. Script not changed.

issues.problem: Only the British spelling 'licence' was accepted; IELTS accepts the American spelling too.
Q1 (spelled surname), Q2 (retirement) and Q3 (date) have no genuine paraphrase in the table.
issues.change: Left vocab off, as the brief allows for names and numbers.

issues.problem: Script note (not changed): the Part 2 speaker says the weir is 'far and away the best place on the river to watch birds'; a few more paraphrased cues in Part 2 audio (e.g. the donor) would make it harder still, but the reworded box now does that job.
issues.change: No action needed; for future recordings, avoid having the speaker say the box wording.
